description:
Send real reference designs from Better Design's library, so you can study how shipped products solved the same design problem before you design the user's own.

`type` picks the collection:
- `app-screens`: product screens of shipped apps, each rebuilt as code (a screenshot when a screen cannot be converted). Pass a few words in `query`, such as "settings" or "invite team", and optionally a `platform`. Each app sends the flow whose name matches best. Pass `language` when the project is React or SwiftUI, so the code comes in that language.
- `html-flows`: shipped flows rebuilt as HTML, so you can read their structure and copy, not only a picture. Pass a few words in `query`, such as "settings" or "create project". Web apps only.
- `app-store-screenshots`: App Store screenshot sets. Pass a `category` such as "Health & Fitness".

Use it before a redesign or a new screen, then design the user's own screen from what the references do well.

category.description: For app-store-screenshots only: an App Store category such as "Productivity". Ignores case.

context.description: Optional. One sentence on WHY you are calling this and what the user asked for (e.g. 'adding nav icons for the fintech dashboard'). Used for usage analytics, and to pick the next step a UI or UX principle answer ends with. It does not change what the tool finds.

language.description: For app-screens only: the language of the code, from what this project builds in. "shopify" sends each screen as a theme section file for sections/. "react", "swiftui" and "shopify" need Pro or a trial. Defaults to "html".

limit.description: How many sets or flows to send. Defaults to 3 sets or 2 flows; at most 6 sets or 3 flows.

query.description: For app-screens and html-flows: words matched against flow names, such as "settings" or "invite team".

type.description: The kind of reference to send: "app-screens", "html-flows" or "app-store-screenshots".
